title: A stream that fails after the model began answering is charged little or nothing against a token budget
foundBy: code review of the token budget, reproduced and widened by session agent

evidence.verified: `make ci` passed at 6d3e7cc, and its replay tier read every lent cell exactly, with none estimated. `go test -race ./internal/lend -count=20` passed 20 runs of `TestAFailedStreamIsChargedByWhetherTheModelAnswered`, `TestAStreamThatFailsMidAnswerSpendsTheBudget`, `TestARateLimitInAStreamSpendsNothing` and `TestAChatChunkOfAnUnknownShapeKeepsItsUsage`. The first test's table holds recorded Responses, Anthropic and chat streams. 22 throttled calls read 22 calls, 0 estimated and 0 tokens under a hard limit of 1. Charging every failure with no usage failed the rate limit test. The rate limit fixture is hand-written, and no live provider failure was run.

resolution: A stream that fails after output began is now charged at least the estimate. A failure before any output costs only what it reported, as a 429 does, whether or not the client stayed to the end. R153e now says so.
details:
The meter charges only the usage a stream reported when that stream ends in its own error. The test used a hard output limit of 1 and five streams of output deltas that end in `response.failed` with null usage. The meter read 5 calls, 5 estimated and 0 tokens, and none was refused. An `error` event in its place gave the same result. Anthropic's `message_start`, then 3,000 deltas, then an `error` event charged 1 output token. The same bytes cost the full estimate when the client left before the stream ended.

A rate limit takes the same path. It arrives as `response.failed` inside a 200, before any output, and Codex sends 22 requests before it fails one such call. Charging each the estimate would cost about 224K input and 180K output on a 46 KB request, for a call that produced nothing. So the charge has to depend on whether output began.
